podcast.title: Rejoining Linkin Park (2002)
podcast.body: Farrell officially rejoined Linkin Park on bass in December 2002, just before the recording of their second album, *Meteora*. His return was made possible by the time secured through the release of the *Reanimation* album. "the reanimation album bought Lincoln Park enough time to record a second CD, and the good news is that it allowed Dave Farrell to rejoin the group on base."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Culinary Skills
podcast.body: Farrell is noted for his cooking abilities, particularly his skill with barbecue. "Guys, also quite the cook, especially when it comes to the barbecue."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Nickname Origin
podcast.body: Dave Farrell acquired the nickname "Phoenix" because he has two prominent phoenix tattoos on his back. "They called him Phoenix because he has two big Phoenix tattoos on his back."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Temporary Departure from Hybrid Theory
podcast.body: In 1999, Farrell temporarily left Hybrid Theory to tour the Christian circuit with his former band, Tasty Snacks. This absence necessitated the hiring of two session bass players for Linkin Park's debut album, *Hybrid Theory*, with Brad Delson filling in for any unplayed parts. "Didn't help that Dave, the bass player, left a tour of the Christian circuit with Tasty Snacks that year."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dave Farrell's Previous Band
xref.body: Tasty Snacks was a Christian Scott punk band that Dave "Phoenix" Farrell was a member of. He temporarily left Hybrid Theory in 1999 to tour the Christian circuit with them. "A former member of a Christian Scott punk band called Tasty Snacks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: UCLA Enrollment
xref.body: Brad Delson attended UCLA, where he became roommates with Dave "Phoenix" Farrell, who would later become Linkin Park's bassist. "Brad enrolled in UCLA, where he became roommates with a bass player named Dave Phoenix Farrell."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
